2.text: Then the Raven runs after the children, who scatter, shouting, “The

3.text: Raven’s eyes are lean, our eyes are fat!”

4.text: A game with almost identically the same details exists among the Rus-

5.text: sians of the Kolyma. In fact, games similar to this are known throughout

6.text: the civilized world. It is hard to tell whether in this particular case it was

7.text: conceived under Russian influence or whether it sprang up independently in

8.text: connection with numerous Raven legends which play an important part in the

9.text: mythology of all the tribes living around Bering Sea.

10.text: Some of the children’s games have an elaborate method of counting the

11.text: points scored. Thus the curious game of “immersing into syphilis,” which I

12.text: mentioned before,¹ has twenty-four points to score. It is played by two per-

13.text: sons, or by two groups of two or three persons each, who try to lasso a

14.text: block of wood lying on the ground or thrown into the air. Each successful

15.text: throw counts one. The counting runs thus: “1. I cover you with eruption;

16.text: 2. I immerse you to the sole; 3. I immerse you to the vamp; 4. I immerse

17.text: you to the instep; 5. I immerse you to the ankle;” and so on until all the

18.text: points corresponding to parts of the human body have been named, from the

19.text: sole of the foot to the crown of the head. The points may be won back one

20.text: by one, or they may be doubled.

21.text: A still more complicated system of counting refers to the succession of

22.text: various incidents of the reindeer-breeding life. It goes like this: “1. I moved

23.text: to the first summer quarters; 2. I castrated the bucks; 3. I moved on to the

24.text: mid-summer quarters; 4. I slaughtered; 5. I prepared boots; 6. I drove (the

25.text: herd) inland; 7. I carried away the kettles; 8. On the grass border; 9. I got

26.text: entangled in the grass; 10. I came out of the grass; 11. In the lower bush;

27.text: 12. I got entangled in the bush; 13. I came out of the bush; 14. In the

28.text: thickness of the bush; 15. I got entangled in the thickness of the bush; 16. I

29.text: came out of the thickness of the bush; 17. On the clearing; 18. I prepared inner

30.text: trousers; 19. I sucked a reindeer-dam; 20. I burned bones.” This point forms

31.text: the climax, and from here begins the return journey, though the names of

32.text: the stages are generally different from those preceding. The total number

33.text: of points is thus thirty-nine. They are often followed by syphilitic counting

34.text: or by another counting having six points and referring to the hunting of wild

35.text: reindeer or seals. Other plans of scoring refer to the slaughtering of reindeer

37.text: Games with elaborate countings are of a lively character. Those who

38.text: are backward are goaded on with jeers. For instance, in the syphilis play

39.text: the winners will assert that the losers have lost their noses withal; or in the

40.text: hunting-play they will taunt the loser with, “You must be hungry [on account

41.text: of the unsuccessful hunt], cut off your boy’s diaper-strings and eat them!” This

42.text: derision often causes games of this character to end in quarrels.
